Add two new Make targets to the existing Makefile that invoke the integration test with appropriate filters and timeouts.

## Changes

1. Add `verify-fast` and `verify-slow` to the .PHONY declaration (currently: help build test install uninstall clean)

```makefile
verify-fast: build ## Run fast-gate template verification (CLI stacks only)
	GOCACHE=$(CURDIR)/.cache/go-build go test -tags=integration -count=1 \
	  -timeout=10m \
	  -run "TestLocalRelease/(go-cli-cobra|python-cli-typer|csharp-cli)" ./test/

verify-slow: build ## Run slow-gate template verification (all stacks)
	GOCACHE=$(CURDIR)/.cache/go-build go test -tags=integration -count=1 \
	  -timeout=20m -run "TestLocalRelease" ./test/
```

## Key Requirements

- Both targets depend on `build` (ensures mkproj binary exists, though TestMain also builds it)
- verify-fast: -timeout=10m, runs only the 3 CLI stacks via -run regex
- verify-slow: -timeout=20m, runs TestLocalRelease (all 6 stacks)
- GOCACHE set to $(CURDIR)/.cache/go-build (already gitignored)
- -count=1 disables test caching (integration tests must always re-run)

## Verification

```bash
make help
```

Expected output includes:
```
verify-fast Run fast-gate template verification (CLI stacks only)
verify-slow Run slow-gate template verification (all stacks)
```

- .PHONY includes verify-fast and verify-slow
- verify-fast regex matches exactly the 3 CLI stacks

title: Vendor shipped v1 catalog assets (golden snapshots + .mkproj-overlay packaging)
description:
## Why this exists
`mkproj init` is required to stay offline and unpack vendored assets rather than run native scaffolders live. The shipped v1 stacks therefore need committed golden snapshots and packaged overlays.

## What to package
Vendor the shipped v1 catalog assets under `templates/golden/`, including the pinned snapshot content and `.mkproj-overlay/` directories for each shipped stack.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] each shipped v1 stack has committed catalog assets under the expected stack key
- [ ] snapshots are pinned and usable offline at init time
- [ ] `.mkproj-overlay/` placement is explicit for every shipped stack

design: Design closed in grill-with-docs 2026-06-20 (ADR-0005). SOURCING: vanilla layer = output of a recipe in sources.yaml with uniform schema {kind: scaffolder|recipe, ordered steps[], gitignore: <stem>, normalize: [...], resolved: {written by update only}}. Single-scaffolder stacks = one-step recipe. go-api-chi is kind:recipe = pinned checkout of golang-standards/project-layout + go mod init + go get of pinned chi/zap/viper/testify; its wired main.go+handler_test live in the OVERLAY, not vanilla. gitignore mapping: Go->Go.gitignore, Python->Python.gitignore, C#->VisualStudio.gitignore, resolved against ONE repo-wide pinned SHA (top-level gitignore_repo key). PACKAGING (path-rule boundary): everything under templates/golden/<key>/.mkproj-overlay/ is the vetted, refresh-immune layer; everything else under the stack dir is vanilla/refreshable. Overlay files may layer INTO vanilla dirs (init composes vanilla-first then overlay-wins). The walking-skeleton test ships in the overlay next to the wiring it exercises (satisfies non-vacuous-test note + uuw). 3tt owns tree shape + vanilla content + declaring overlay slots; x2k/02o/ud1 own specific overlay files placed within it.
notes: Walking-skeleton model (ADR-0005): shipped artifact must RUN end-to-end with a green test after init; this is the acceptance guarantee on composed vanilla+overlay, not a third layer.

title: Implement mkproj update steps interpreter (run/checkout/strip)
description:
## Why this exists
ADR-0005 commits mkproj update (maintainer path) to executing a recipe's ordered steps[] from sources.yaml. Each row's recipe is a uniform schema with step verbs that need an interpreter. ## What to build
A small step interpreter invoked by mkproj update that executes, in order, the step verbs declared on a sources.yaml row:
- run: <shell> — invoke a pinned native scaffolder / toolchain command in the temp build dir (e.g. cobra-cli init, go mod init, go get ...)
- checkout: <repo> + ref: <SHA> — clone a pinned git ref into the temp dir
- strip: [globs] — remove paths (.git, README, docs, examples) from the checked-out tree
Steps run in a temp dir; output becomes the vanilla layer (before normalization, ADR-0006). Fails loud naming any missing tool (prompt-render-contract §8).

- [ ] run/checkout/strip verbs execute in declared order against a sources.yaml row

- [ ] interpreter runs only on the maintainer update path, never at init
- [ ] output feeds the ADR-0006 normalization pass (interpreter does not normalize)
notes: Step schema per ADR-0005: a sources.yaml row's steps[] use two verbs — 'checkout' (clone a pinned git ref; optional per-step 'strip:' removes paths like .git/README/docs) and 'run' (invoke a pinned scaffolder/toolchain command). 'strip' is a sub-key of a checkout step, NOT a third top-level verb. Single-scaffolder stacks are a one-step recipe through the same interpreter (no shape branching).

description:
## Why this exists

title: Generated test repos clone forge's own Beads database (root cause of red main CI)
description:
## Problem

`fast-gate` and every `slow-gate` job have been red on `main` since at least 2026-11-13. The log shows `forge init` failing at `bd init` with `schema version mismatch: database is at v66, binary knows up to v53`.

The schema mismatch is the symptom. The cause is test isolation:

1. `test/local_release_test.go` lines 33-34 set `runtimeWorkspaceRoot = repoRoot`.
2. `test/runtime_workspace.go` lines 8-14 therefore create each generated repo at `<forge>/.cache/local-release/forge-runtime-*`, inside the forge checkout.
3. `internal/init/init.go` runs `git init` and then `bd init` there (lines 34 and 71).
4. bd loads configuration by walking up from the current directory to the first `.beads/config.yaml`. It finds forge's own file, whose `sync.remote` points at the forge repository.
5. `bd init` treats a configured `sync.remote` as a bootstrap and clones forge's issue database into the generated test repo.

With bd 1.1.0 that clone fails on the newer schema. With bd 1.3.4 (the CI pinning ticket in this epic) it succeeds, which turns CI green but leaves every generated test repo silently carrying a copy of forge's issues. A generated repo must start with an empty issue database.

## Change

Make the runtime workspace used by the `TestLocalRelease` and upgrade end-to-end tests independent of forge's Beads configuration. Use the first of these that works, and nothing more:

1. Create the runtime directories outside the forge tree: in `test/runtime_workspace.go`, use the existing `os.MkdirTemp("", ...)` branch for these tests instead of a directory under `repoRoot`.
2. If a test depends on the workspace being under the repo (check the comment where `runtimeWorkspaceRoot` is set), keep the location and instead set `BEADS_DIR` for the `forge init` child process to the generated repo's own `.beads` directory.

Do not change `internal/init/init.go` behaviour for real users, and do not change forge's `.beads/config.yaml`.

## Files

- `test/runtime_workspace.go`, `test/local_release_test.go`
- another file under `test/` only if it sets the same workspace root

## Rules

1. Change only the files listed. If another file must change, stop and report it in this ticket.
2. Fix the isolation only. Do not refactor the test helpers or add new tests beyond the one assertion below.
3. Do not skip, disable or loosen any test.
4. If neither approach works, stop and report what you tried with the output.
5. Done means: the scenarios pass, the change is committed and pushed, and this ticket is closed with `bd close`.

title: Pin forge's own CI workflow and bats to exact versions
description:
## Context

`forge` is a Go CLI that scaffolds repositories from embedded assets. What a generated repo receives comes from three layers, applied in this order (`internal/scaffold/writer.go`):

1. `templates/common/` - shared assets for every stack.
2. `templates/golden/<stack>/` - the "vanilla" layer captured from an upstream generator.
3. `templates/golden/<stack>/.forge-overlay/` - forge's vetted layer. It wins on any path collision.

Version values are literal text in these files. Nothing injects them from Go code. Files ending in `.tmpl` are rendered and lose the suffix. For the TypeScript stacks the overlay `package.json.tmpl` replaces the vanilla one, so the overlay file is the one that ships. No lockfiles ship (ADR-0014), so a range resolves to whatever the registry serves on the day of `forge init`; that is why this epic pins exact versions.

Background reading if a term is unclear: `docs/SPEC.md` section 15, `docs/adr/0005-*`, `docs/adr/0014-*`, `docs/adr/0020-*`, `CONTEXT.md`.

Versions in this ticket were looked up on 2026-11-18 from the upstream registries.

## Goal

Forge's only workflow uses major-tag actions, an unpinned mise in two of three jobs, a floating runner and beads 1.1.0. Pin all of it.

## Changes

In `.github/workflows/verify-templates.yml`, in all three jobs (`unit-tests`, `fast-gate`, `slow-gate`):

| Line today | Replace with |
|---|---|
| `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` | `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` |
| `uses: actions/checkout@v4` | `uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1` |
| `uses: actions/setup-go@v5` | `uses: actions/setup-go@d8cbb8045d7f43706b9177cceb36c1f91a6644d5 # v7.1.0` |
| `uses: jdx/mise-action@v2` | `uses: jdx/mise-action@236a21c3b91f5db6d4e174b348674a0f0caac06d # v5.2.9` |

Every `jdx/mise-action` step gets a `with:` block containing `version: 2026.11.9` and `env: false`. The `unit-tests` job keeps its existing `install: false`.

Why `env: false`: since mise-action v3 the action exports mise `[env]` to later steps. Forge's `.config/mise/conf.d/otel.toml` sets `OTEL_*` variables, which would leak into the `go test` steps. `env: false` keeps today's behaviour.

Beads, in both `Install bd (beads)` steps:

- `BEADS_VERSION: 1.3.4`
- Download URL host path changes from `steveyegge/beads` to `gastownhall/beads`.
- `BEADS_SHA256: 175c26904bde3ff9168d2282ff6b56f17b17f60c22fa5acb3dacc9fb3465303a` (from the release's `checksums.txt`, for `beads_1.3.4_linux_amd64.tar.gz`).

Why 1.3.4: forge's shared Beads database is at schema v66. bd 1.1.0 knows only v53 and fails on it, which is why `fast-gate` and `slow-gate` are red on `main`. bd 1.3.0 through 1.3.4 know exactly v66. Do not use a 1.4 release candidate: it migrates the schema one-way.

This ticket also resolves two existing issues; close them with this one: `agentic_template_start-mcu` (pin mise in every job) and `agentic_template_start-0y9` (fast-gate schema mismatch).

In `mise.toml` line 10: `bats = "1.14.0"`.

In `test/verify_templates_workflow_test.go` lines 34-37: update the four asserted strings to the new `uses:` lines.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/verify-templates.yml`
- `mise.toml`
- `test/verify_templates_workflow_test.go`

## Known upstream changes (no action needed beyond the above)

- checkout v5+ and setup-go v6+ run on Node 24 and need runner v2.327.1 or later; GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` meets that.
- mise-action v5.2.0 changed its cache key, so the first run misses the cache once.

## Rules

1. Change only the files listed under "Files". If another file must change for the gate to pass, stop and report it in this ticket.
2. Use exactly the versions listed. Do not pick a newer one, even if one has been released since.
3. Write exact pins: no `^`, `~`, `>=`, `~=`, `latest`, or major-only tags. GitHub Actions use the full commit SHA plus a `# vX.Y.Z` comment.
4. Do not run `forge update`; it would drop hand-maintained manifest lines. Edit manifests by hand.
5. Do not add lockfiles, Renovate/Dependabot, a central versions file, helper scripts, or new tests. Only update existing assertions.
6. Do not refactor, rename, reformat, or remove unused dependencies.
7. Update a test only where it asserts a version string this ticket changes.
8. For a "Verify first" step, run the stated command and use its result. If the result contradicts this ticket, stop and report.
9. If a gate fails for a reason this ticket does not predict, stop and report with the output. Do not skip tests or loosen assertions.

11. Done means: every scenario under acceptance criteria passes, the change is committed and pushed, and this ticket is closed with `bd close`.

title: Pin and upgrade every upstream version forge deploys
description:
## Why

Forge ships version pins into every generated repository, and they have drifted. Many are ranges or `latest`, no lockfiles ship (ADR-0014), and nothing detects staleness, so a repo generated today and one generated next month can get different dependencies. Most shipped versions are hand-maintained in manifests and overlays; `forge update` only regenerates the three Go vanilla layers.

## Outcome

Every upstream version forge deploys is an exact pin at the current release, and each breaking major is handled in its own ticket.

## Decisions (made 2026-11-18)

- Exact versions everywhere: no ranges, no `latest`.
- GitHub Actions pinned to a commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment.
- One ticket per breaking major; minor and patch bumps batched per stack.
- One-time pass: no Renovate or Dependabot.

Versions were fetched on 2026-11-18 from the Go module proxy, npm, PyPI, NuGet, Docker Hub, MCR and GitHub. Items marked *verify* could not be confirmed then and are "Verify first" steps in their ticket.

## Order of work

title: Bump forge's own go.mod to current patch releases
description:
## Context

`forge` is a Go CLI that scaffolds repositories from embedded assets. What a generated repo receives comes from three layers, applied in this order (`internal/scaffold/writer.go`):

1. `templates/common/` - shared assets for every stack.
2. `templates/golden/<stack>/` - the "vanilla" layer captured from an upstream generator.
3. `templates/golden/<stack>/.forge-overlay/` - forge's vetted layer. It wins on any path collision.

Version values are literal text in these files. Nothing injects them from Go code. Files ending in `.tmpl` are rendered and lose the suffix. For the TypeScript stacks the overlay `package.json.tmpl` replaces the vanilla one, so the overlay file is the one that ships. No lockfiles ship (ADR-0014), so a range resolves to whatever the registry serves on the day of `forge init`; that is why this epic pins exact versions.

Background reading if a term is unclear: `docs/SPEC.md` section 15, `docs/adr/0005-*`, `docs/adr/0014-*`, `docs/adr/0020-*`, `CONTEXT.md`.

Versions in this ticket were looked up on 2026-11-18 from the upstream registries.

## Goal

Bring forge's own Go modules to current releases and correct the stale Go version in the contributor docs.

## Changes

Run, in this order, from the repo root:

```bash
go mod edit -go=1.26.11
go get github.com/mattn/go-isatty@v0.0.24 golang.org/x/sync@v0.25.0 golang.org/x/sys@v0.50.0 golang.org/x/text@v0.44.0
go mod tidy
```

`go mod tidy` will also remove the wrong `// indirect` markers on `github.com/charmbracelet/huh` and `github.com/mattn/go-isatty`, which the source imports directly. That is expected. Do not hand-edit other indirect lines; accept what `go mod tidy` writes.

Do not change `github.com/charmbracelet/huh` here. Its v2 migration is a separate ticket.

Docs: replace `1.24.x` with `1.26.x` in `README.md` line 56 and `AGENTS.md` line 7 (`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`).

This ticket also resolves two existing issues; close them with this one: `agentic_template_start-28p` (go.mod indirect markers) and `agentic_template_start-7jd` (docs say Go 1.24.x).

## Files

- `go.mod`, `go.sum`
- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`

## Rules

1. Change only the files listed under "Files". If another file must change for the gate to pass, stop and report it in this ticket.
2. Use exactly the versions listed. Do not pick a newer one, even if one has been released since.
3. Write exact pins: no `^`, `~`, `>=`, `~=`, `latest`, or major-only tags. GitHub Actions use the full commit SHA plus a `# vX.Y.Z` comment.
4. Do not run `forge update`; it would drop hand-maintained manifest lines. Edit manifests by hand.
5. Do not add lockfiles, Renovate/Dependabot, a central versions file, helper scripts, or new tests. Only update existing assertions.
6. Do not refactor, rename, reformat, or remove unused dependencies.
7. Update a test only where it asserts a version string this ticket changes.
8. For a "Verify first" step, run the stated command and use its result. If the result contradicts this ticket, stop and report.
9. If a gate fails for a reason this ticket does not predict, stop and report with the output. Do not skip tests or loosen assertions.
10. If a scenario needs a tool your environment lacks (docker, dotnet, node), say which scenario you could not run. Do not report it as passed.
11. Done means: every scenario under acceptance criteria passes, the change is committed and pushed, and this ticket is closed with `bd close`.

  Then every package passes

title: Record upstream upgrades deliberately not taken in the November 2026 pass
description:
## Purpose

A record, not implementation work. These upstream versions were found during the November 2026 survey and deliberately left alone. The next survey should start here. Close this ticket only when each item has been re-evaluated or split into its own ticket.

## Items

| Item | Available | Why not now |
|---|---|---|
| TypeScript 7 | 7.0.2 | typescript-eslint caps below 6.1, Angular 22 at 6.0.x, svelte-check and SvelteKit 3 at 6. Revisit when those accept 7. |
| .NET 11 | SDK 11.0.100 | Short-term support (ends 2028-11). .NET 10 is the LTS line. Needs a decision on whether generated repos should track STS releases. |
| htmx 4 | 4.0.2 on the `next` tag | Separate major line, not yet `latest`. |
| beads 1.4 | 1.4.0-rc.3 | Release candidate with a one-way schema migration. |
| xunit.v3 | 4.0.3 | Different package id and test platform; a migration, not a bump. |
| create-vite 9 | 9.3.4 | Generator major. Vite itself stays on 8, and the vanilla layer is captured by hand. |
| uv 0.13 | 0.13.9 | Since 0.12, `uv init` emits a `uv_build` backend and `src/` layout, which conflicts with the hatchling flat layout in the three Python stacks. `uv init --no-package` is the documented opt-out. The three recipes also record different uv versions (0.11.8 twice, 0.8.17 once). |
| cobra-cli | v1.3.0 (latest) | The recipe runs whatever `cobra-cli` is on PATH; it is not pinned in the command. |
| `@opentelemetry/browser-instrumentation` | separate `opentelemetry-browser` project | Upstream marks `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-fetch` deprecated in favour of it. The fetch instrumentation still works on the 3.x line, so the stacks keep it for now. |
| Docker image digests | - | Images are pinned by exact tag, not by digest. |

## Unused dependencies noticed

Listed in manifests but never imported by template code. Removing them changes what generated repos receive, so it needs its own decision:

- go-api-chi: viper, testify, zap
- csharp-cli: System.CommandLine
- .NET test projects: NSubstitute
- Python stacks: pytest-mock

## Unpinned at runtime

`forge init` runs `bd`, `instill`, `mise`, `lefthook`, `git`, `gh`, `go`, `npm`, `pip` and `docker` from PATH with no version check (`internal/init/init.go` lines 71-131). No drift detection (Renovate, Dependabot) is configured; that was a deliberate choice for this pass.

title: Orchestrate the upstream upgrade backlog from a cloud session: dispatch, review, merge and repeat
description:
## Purpose

This ticket is the entry point for an orchestrating agent running in a cloud session. Point an orchestrator at it and it works through every open child of epic `agentic_template_start-3xw`: it dispatches one subagent per ticket, in parallel wherever the dependency graph allows, reviews each result, merges accepted work into `main`, refreshes its branch, and starts the next wave.

You are the orchestrator. You do not implement tickets yourself. You dispatch, review, integrate, merge and report.

## How a cloud session shapes this

- A cloud session can push to exactly one branch: the one it was assigned. All work therefore lands through that one branch, one pull request per wave.
- Parallelism happens inside the container: each subagent works in its own git worktree on a local branch that is never pushed.
- A cloud session cannot push the shared Beads database (`bd dolt push` is refused). Ticket state is therefore recorded in git, in commit subjects on `main`, and mirrored into a local Beads copy.
- The container is ephemeral. Everything that matters must be on `main` or in the open pull request before you stop.

## Decisions already made by the repository owner (do not revisit)

- Work that passes the orchestrator's review is good enough to merge. The orchestrator merges its own wave pull request into `main` once the review has passed and CI is green. The owner authorised this on 2026-11-18 by directing an orchestrator to this ticket. If your session's rules require the user's direct instruction before merging, confirm once at the start and then proceed without asking again.
- One pull request per wave, containing one commit per ticket.
- The dependency graph in Beads is the schedule. Do not reorder it and do not start a ticket that `bd ready` does not list.
- Each child ticket's own Rules section binds the subagent. This ticket does not loosen any of them.

## Setup (once per session)

1. Install `bd` 1.3.4. Other versions cannot read the shared database (1.1.0) or would migrate it one-way (1.4).

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL -o /tmp/beads.tar.gz https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/download/v1.3.4/beads_1.3.4_linux_amd64.tar.gz
   echo "175c26904bde3ff9168d2282ff6b56f17b17f60c22fa5acb3dacc9fb3465303a  /tmp/beads.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
   mkdir -p /tmp/bd && tar -xzf /tmp/beads.tar.gz -C /tmp/bd
   install -m 0755 "$(find /tmp/bd -type f -name bd | head -n 1)" "$HOME/.local/bin/bd"
   ```

2. `bd bootstrap --dry-run` must say "clone from remote"; then `bd bootstrap --yes`. This gives you a local copy of the shared database. `bd bootstrap` rewrites `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore` and `.beads/metadata.json`; run `git checkout -- .beads/` afterwards and never commit those changes.
3. Reconcile with git, because earlier sessions could not push Beads state: run `git log origin/main --format=%s`, and for every child ticket whose ID appears in a subject as `(agentic_template_start-3xw.N)`, run `bd close` on it locally if it is still open.
4. Read the epic: `bd show agentic_template_start-3xw`.
5. Install the toolchain prerequisites, so every acceptance scenario can be run in this container. A fresh cloud container has Go, uv, npm and the Docker client, but no mise, no .NET SDK and no running Docker daemon. Verified on 2026-11-18:

   ```bash
   export MISE_VERSION=v2026.11.9 MISE_INSTALL_PATH=$HOME/.local/bin/mise
   curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh
   mise --version                      # 2026.11.9
   dockerd > /tmp/dockerd.log 2>&1 &   # the container runs as root
   until docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done
   ```

   mise then supplies every SDK at the version a ticket pins: `mise install` inside a scaffolded repo, or for a one-off check `mise exec dotnet@10.0.404 -- dotnet --version`. Do not install SDKs any other way (no apt, no install scripts), so the version tested is the version pinned. Subagents share this container, so this is done once, by you, before the first wave.

   If mise or the Docker daemon cannot be installed or started, stop and report. Do not run the loop without them.

## The loop

Repeat until no child of the epic other than this ticket and `.23` is open:

1. Start from a clean branch: fetch `origin/main` and restart your assigned branch from it (see Refreshing the branch).
2. `bd ready`, keeping only children of `agentic_template_start-3xw`. Skip this ticket and `.23` (a backlog record with no implementation). Take up to 5. This is the wave.
3. First wave: it must contain `.1` and `.24` and nothing else. CI on `main` is red until they land, so no other work can show a green run before then.
4. Dispatch one subagent per ticket in a single step so they run concurrently, each with worktree isolation, using the brief below.
5. Review each result (see Review). Do not trust a subagent's summary; read its diff. If a review fails, send the same subagent the specific findings; at most 2 rounds.
6. For each ticket that passed, in ticket-number order, bring it onto your assigned branch as exactly one commit: `git merge --squash <worktree-branch>` then commit with the subject `<ticket title> (<ticket-id>)`. A ticket that did not pass is left out of the wave; see Failure handling.
7. Run `GOCACHE=$PWD/.cache/go-build go test ./... -count=1` on the combined branch. If it fails, find which ticket's commit causes it, drop that commit from the wave, and treat that ticket as a failed review.
8. Push the branch and open a draft pull request titled `Upgrade wave <n>: <ticket suffixes>`. The description lists each ticket with its acceptance results and a "Not verified" section. Subscribe to the pull request's activity.
9. Wait for CI. When every check is green, mark the pull request ready and merge it with a merge commit (not squash), so each ticket stays one revertible commit on `main`.
10. `bd close` each merged ticket locally. Try `bd dolt push` once; if it is refused, carry on and note it for the final report.

If CI is red on the wave pull request: find the root cause. If one ticket's commit is responsible, have its subagent fix it on the worktree branch, re-review, and replace that commit; or drop the commit from the wave and treat the ticket as a failed review. Never merge with a red check, never re-run a job more than once, never skip or disable a test.

## Refreshing the branch

After a wave pull request has merged, your assigned branch holds only merged history. Restart it under the same name from the latest `main`:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git checkout -B <assigned-branch> origin/main
git push --force-with-lease -u origin <assigned-branch>
```

Do this only when the previous pull request shows as merged. A new wave gets a new pull request. Because every wave starts from a `main` that already contains its predecessors, there is no stacking and no "merge after" ordering.

## Subagent brief

Give each subagent exactly this, filled in, followed by the full output of `bd show <TICKET-ID>`. It has no other context, and the local Beads database is not available inside a worktree, so the ticket text must be in the brief.

```
You are implementing one Beads ticket in the forge repository, in your own
git worktree on a local branch. Do not push, do not open a pull request,
and do not switch branches.

1. Read the whole ticket below (ID <TICKET-ID>), including Rules and
   acceptance criteria. The ticket is the specification; follow it exactly.
   Where a ticket rule says "push" or "close the ticket", do not: commit
   locally and report instead. The orchestrator does the rest.
2. Make the changes the ticket lists, and nothing else.
3. Run every scenario in the ticket's acceptance criteria. For each one,
   record the command you ran and its result. mise and a Docker daemon are
   already set up in this container: get any SDK with `mise install` in a
   scaffolded repo or `mise exec <tool>@<version> -- <command>`, and do not
   install SDKs any other way. If a scenario still cannot be run, say
   exactly what failed and mark it "not run".
4. Commit your work on your local branch.
5. Report back: your branch name; for each acceptance scenario: passed,
   failed, or not run and why; every file you changed; and anything in the
   ticket that turned out to be wrong.

If a ticket rule tells you to stop and report, stop and report. Do not work
around it. Do not run any `bd` command.

--- TICKET ---
<paste the output of bd show here>
```

## Review

Accept a ticket only if all of these hold. Check them yourself from the diff and by running commands, not from the subagent's report.

1. Files: `git diff --name-only origin/main...<worktree-branch>` is a subset of the ticket's Files list.
2. Versions: every pin in the diff equals the version the ticket names. No `^`, `~`, `>=`, `~=`, `latest` or major-only tag on an item the ticket pins.
3. Scope: no refactors, renames, reformatting, new tooling, new tests beyond updated assertions, or removed dependencies.
4. Tests: none skipped, deleted or loosened. An assertion changes only where it asserts a version string the ticket changes.
5. Suite: run `GOCACHE=$PWD/.cache/go-build go test ./... -count=1` on the worktree branch yourself. It passes.
6. Acceptance: every scenario is reported with a command and a result. Re-run at least one scenario yourself, choosing the one most specific to the ticket.
7. Every scenario was actually run. The setup installs mise and starts Docker, so "the tool is missing" is not an acceptable reason. A scenario that could not be run for another reason (for example it needs a real browser) is a review failure unless the Go suite passes, CI is green and every other scenario of the ticket passed; in that case accept it and list the scenario in the pull request's "Not verified" section and in the final report.

The review passing is the merge decision. There is no further human gate.

## Failure handling

- A subagent stops because a ticket rule says "stop and report": do not override it. Record what it reported with `bd update <id> --append-notes`, flag the ticket with `bd human <id>`, leave it open and out of the wave, and carry on.
- Review still fails after 2 fix rounds, or CI stays red because of the ticket: same as above.
- A ticket's instructions prove wrong (a line number moved, a version no longer exists): small factual corrections that the ticket's goal clearly implies are fine; record them in the commit body. Anything that changes scope or a decision goes to `bd human`.
- Tickets blocked by a flagged ticket stay blocked. Do not start them.
- If nothing is ready and tickets remain open, stop the loop and report.

## Finishing

Beads state made in this session is local, so the report must reach the owner through git:

1. Post one comment on the last wave pull request with the final report: every child ticket and its state (merged in which pull request, flagged with the reason, or not started because blocked), every scenario that was not verified, and the exact `bd close ...` and `bd human ...` commands the owner should run to bring the shared database in line, unless a `bd dolt push` succeeded.
2. Give the same report as your final message.
3. Do not close this ticket yourself unless a `bd dolt push` succeeded and every child except `.23` is closed.

## Rules

1. Never implement a ticket yourself, and never review your own implementation.
2. Merge only your own wave pull requests, only after the review passed for every ticket in them, and only with every CI check green.
3. Never start a ticket that `bd ready` does not list.
4. Never skip, disable or loosen a test, and never accept a diff that does.
5. Force-push only to restart your assigned branch after its pull request has merged. Never rewrite a branch with an open pull request.
6. Push to no branch other than your assigned one. Do not add workflows or other mechanisms to push elsewhere.
7. Do not create new tickets for scope the epic does not contain. Record such findings in the final report.
8. Do not edit a child ticket's pins, files list, rules or acceptance criteria.
